title: Prune dead code and replace leaky caches in GPU autoscaler / capacity planner
creator: Ayesha Malik
description:
Summary:
Observed long-term heap growth and periodic OOMs in the capacity-planner process for large GPU fleets. Investigation points to several legacy caches, snake-oil heuristics around lease windows, and unused reconciliation branches that keep references alive. This ticket consolidates the diagnostic findings, removes dead/unused codepaths, replaces ad-hoc caches with bounded LRU caches backed by metrics and sampling, and simplifies the node lifecycle state transitions to reduce retention and GC pressure.

Scope:
- Trim dead reconciliation branches introduced during prior multi-pool experiments.
- Replace unbounded in-memory maps used for lease/history tracking with size-limited LRU caches and explicit eviction.
- Remove legacy 'sticky reservation' flags that are unused by downstream callers.
- Add visibility (prometheus metrics + p50/p90/p99 retention size gauges) for the planner's cache sizes.
- Validate that autoscaler cold-start latency does not regress under heavy churn.

Why now:
- Reduces production OOM incidents and pager noise.
- Improves memory footprint to allow denser colocated control-plane services on management nodes.
- Lowers GC overhead and improves reconciliation throughput under high-churn workloads (scale-ups/downs).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Capacity-planner memory usage reduced by >=40% on synthetic high-churn test over 2h run.
2) No unbounded cache growth observed in 24h soak in staging.
3) All removed code paths gated by feature flags or proven unused in telemetry; PRs include removal tests.
4) New metrics published: planner_cache_items, planner_evictions_total, planner_reconcile_duration_seconds (summary).
5) Regression test shows no >5% increase in median reconcile latency and no >10% increase in tail latency.
6) Rollout plan documented and can be reverted within 30 minutes if issues seen.

progress_updates: 2026-01-22: Initial heap profiles attached to internal drive collection link; pattern shows growth correlated with 'leaseHistoryMap' entries.
2026-01-29: Reproduction harness (k8s churn simulator) created; reproduces memory growth within ~45 minutes on a 1000-node fleet simulation.
2026-02-08: Spike of activity revealed a hidden retention chain from 'legacyReservationIndex' that referenced Node objects held by reconcile context; flagged as candidate for removal.
2026-02-18: PR #1227 implemented LRU cache and eviction metrics; unit tests added. Synthetic soak shows 28% reduction in RSS on 1h run. Needs more evictions tuning.
2026-03-02: Benchmarks updated; p95 reconcile latency unchanged, p99 improved by ~6%. Found one case where eviction caused subsequent CPU spike; added throttled eviction backoff.
2026-03-10: Canary rollout on staging-control-plane: 6/6 pods stable after 12h, no OOMs, cache sizes stable. Ready to prepare prod rollout patch and run extended soak.
2026-03-10: Diego requested review from Jin and Sam on PR #1259 for dead code removal and memory optimization.\n
blockers: - Need final sign-off from infra security on removal of reservation telemetry shim.\n- Dependency on ENG-100214 to land API contract change that allows pruning obsolete reservation flags.\n- Load-test infra quota limited; extended soak waits on additional capacity request (Q1287).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for LRU eviction correctness.
- Integration job: 1000-node churn for 4h with heap sampling every 5m.
- Load test: 10k reconcile events/min for 1h comparing baseline and patched planner.
- Verify prometheus metrics and set alert threshold for planner_cache_items > 5000.
rollout_plan:
- Merge behind feature flag 'planner_lru_cache_v2'.
- Canary: enable on 10% of control-plane pods for 1h, verify no errors and stable memory.
- Ramp to 50% for 6h with continuous heap sampling.
- Full rollout if soak passes; monitor for 24h with oncall alerting and a revert patch ready.
- Post-rollout: schedule follow-up ticket to remove flag after 4 weeks if stable.
post_launch_checks:
- Verify planner_cache_items and planner_evictions_total metrics in production dashboards.
- Confirm no increase in reconcile errors over baseline.
- Heap profile comparison between pre-change and 24h post-change.
- Close any child tickets created for minor bugfixes.
notes: - Avoid premature optimization: keep eviction policy deterministic and simple.\n- Consider future work: migrate history storage to small persisted store if retention >24h is required.\n- Coordinate with Dedicated team to ensure changes don't affect reserved capacity heuristics.
